summary: The sample implements the core requested functionality: a Node.js + Express + Mongoose service that stores GeoJSON Point locations, creates a 2dsphere index, exposes GET /nearby which runs a $geoNear aggregation and returns opening hours and stock. Seed, verify and README quickstart were provided and verified against the live Azure DocumentDB cluster. Findings are mostly documentation, hardening and a few best-practice gaps (retries, pagination, explicit connection options, production index build guidance, tests, and cleanup instructions). Several product-team best-practices are present and discoverable in the installed DocumentDB skills; two common Mongoose/MongoDB priors (autoIndex and lat/lon input validation) had no service-specific public guidance in the discovery step and remain gaps.

requirement_results.requirement: Define a Mongoose model for stores in a Node.js service whose location is stored as a GeoJSON Point (type "Point" with a [longitude, latitude] coordinates array) in Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/store.js: lines 3-8 (StoreSchema definition with location: { type: { type: String, enum: ['Point'] }, coordinates: [Number] } )

requirement_results.requirement: Create a 2dsphere index on the GeoJSON location field in code (e.g. declared on the Mongoose schema with schema.index({ location: '2dsphere' })).
Expose a /nearby HTTP endpoint that accepts a latitude, a longitude and a radius as inputs (e.g. query parameters).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js: lines 5-10 (route GET /nearby and parsing req.query.lat, req.query.lon, req.query.radiusMeters)

requirement_results.requirement: Have the /nearby handler run a $geoNear aggregation through Mongoose against Azure DocumentDB, using the request's latitude and longitude as the near point and the request's radius as the maximum distance.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js: lines 16-24 (pipeline with $geoNear using near: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [lon, lat] } and maxDistance: radius) and line 36 (Store.aggregate(pipeline).exec())

requirement_results.requirement: Return the matching stores ordered by distance from the request point, nearest first (the $geoNear stage supplies the ordering).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js: pipeline uses $geoNear which supplies ordering; response returned on line 36-37 (res.json({ count: results.length, results })). Verification script returned sorted results per build logs (events.jsonl: verify run showing distanceMeters).

requirement_results.requirement: Include each store's opening hours and stock availability in the /nearby response, taken from the stored store document (e.g. openingHours and stock fields).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js: $project includes opening_hours and stock (lines 26-31). Model defines opening_hours and stock in app/src/models/store.js (lines 9-19).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/index.js: lines 13-19 (reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and fails if missing). app/.env.example contains a placeholder (no real secret).

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI with a placeholder (file present). README documents how to copy .env.example to .env.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector indexes are created in the repository (no createIndexes with cosmosSearch/cosmosSearchOptions for vector found in code). app/seed/seed.js and model files contain only GeoJSON fields.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If the sample will include vector search, add an explicit step to the starter prompt (or skill) to create vector indexes with dimensions matching the chosen embedding model and add those parameters to the seed/migration script and README. Prefer adding a rule to the documentdb-vector-search skill or a README section saying exactly which embedding model and dimension the sample uses.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector indexes or vector-index tuning guidance in repository; README does not mention vector indexes.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If vector search is added, include an explicit README section describing index engine choice (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF), parameters (lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree) for small sample vs larger datasets, and an example createIndexes JSON.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/index.js: mongoose.connect(URI, { dbName: 'sample_retail_20' }) is called once at startup (lines 21-29); Mongoose models reuse that connection.

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed/seed.js: uses Store.updateOne(..., { upsert: true }) for each seed item (lines 23-26) and calls Store.createIndexes() (lines 29-31). Verified by build run (events.jsonl shows 'Upserted ...' and 'Indexes ensured').

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If a /search endpoint is required, add it to the starter prompt and implement explicit validation (400 for empty query) and error handling around embedding calls (return 502/503 with a clear error on embedding failures).

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No /search or vector/embedding code exists in repo to produce similarity scores.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If adding semantic/vector search, include similarity score in the aggregation pipeline response (e.g., distance/score field), and document it in README and API responses.

requirement_results.evidence: This is a Node.js project. package.json lists dependencies with caret ranges (app/package.json lines 15-19) but package-lock.json is present (locks installed package versions). No Python requirements.txt is present.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either (A) change the checklist to accept package-lock.json for Node projects, or (B) pin dependency versions precisely in package.json (no caret) and include package-lock.json. Smallest immediate fix for this repo: commit package-lock.json (already present) and add a README note that package-lock.json pins the dependencies.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: No test files present; no in-memory or mock tests provided. README does not document test requirements.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests that use an in-memory MongoDB (mongodb-memory-server) or mocks, and document how to run them without a live cluster in README.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC files (Bicep/Terraform/ARM) present; repo contains no Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters template or Terraform module.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an IaC template (Bicep or Terraform) that creates Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters for tier, storage and region, or provide a short example in README linking to the official quickstart template.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: README includes what it shows, prerequisites and quickstart (install, seed, start) but contains no explicit clean-up steps (e.g., how to remove created documents/collections or how to delete test resources).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'Clean-up' section to README describing how to drop the stores collection, remove sample documents, and any cloud cleanup steps (if IaC provided, show `az`/Bicep/Terraform destroy commands).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README title and body refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' (app/README.md lines 1 and 3). package.json/description also uses 'Azure DocumentDB'.

checks.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable at runtime and do not commit cluster URIs or secrets to source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
checks.evidence: app/src/index.js lines 13-19 (reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and exits if missing); app/.env.example contains a placeholder example (app/.env.example line 3).

checks.practice: Always connect to Azure DocumentDB with TLS enabled and validate server certificates in production (do not disable certificate verification in production).
checks.evidence: app/.env.example includes an example connection string with ssl=true (app/.env.example line 3). app/src/index.js reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and relies on the connection string provided by the operator.

checks.practice: Use least-privilege credentials for application access (prefer Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or per-app users with minimal roles rather than cluster admin/root credentials).
checks.evidence: The sample reads DOCUMENTDB_URI without guidance on least-privilege credentials; neither README nor seed scripts create a limited user account or state that the provided string should be least-privileged.
checks.fix: Add README guidance and an example for creating/using a least-privilege DB user or Microsoft Entra ID authentication. Include a short shell/az command or mongo shell snippet showing how to create a per-app user.

checks.practice: Create a single MongoClient / Mongoose connection and reuse it for the process (singleton client pattern).
checks.evidence: app/src/index.js calls mongoose.connect once at startup (lines 21-29); Mongoose models use that connection.

checks.practice: Set sensible connection and socket timeouts and configure the connection pool (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS).
checks.evidence: app/src/index.js uses mongoose.connect(URI, { dbName: 'sample_retail_20' }) with no explicit pool or timeout options; no socketTimeoutMS or serverSelectionTimeoutMS are set in code.
checks.fix: Pass sensible connection options from env (e.g., { maxPoolSize: parseInt(process.env.DB_MAX_POOL||'10'), socketTimeoutMS: 30000, serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000 }) or document recommended defaults in README and the documentdb-connection skill.

checks.practice: Model GeoJSON Points as objects with type:'Point' and coordinates:[longitude, latitude] and validate the type and coordinate array shape in your schema.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/store.js: location field defined as { type: { type: String, enum: ['Point'] }, coordinates: { type: [Number], required: true } } (lines 5-8). Seed data uses coordinates as [lon, lat].

checks.practice: Create a 2dsphere index on the GeoJSON location field before relying on geospatial queries and verify the index exists on the collection.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/store.js defines StoreSchema.index({ location: '2dsphere' }) (line 23). Build run verified indexes via MCP list (events.jsonl tool documentdb_list_indexes returned location_2dsphere). Seed script calls Store.createIndexes() (seed/seed.js line 29-31).

checks.practice: Create required indexes as part of deployment or controlled migration steps rather than relying on Mongoose autoIndex in production; use autoIndex only in development.
checks.evidence: Repository includes a seed script that calls Store.createIndexes() (seed/seed.js lines 29-31).
checks.fix: Disable Mongoose autoIndex in production via mongoose.connect options or config (autoIndex:false) so production doesn't rely on autoIndex; smallest change: set autoIndex:false when NODE_ENV==='production'.

checks.practice: Use an aggregation with a $geoNear stage (supplying near: { type:'Point', coordinates:[lng,lat] }, distanceField and maxDistance in meters) to both filter by radius and rank results by distance.
checks.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js pipeline includes $geoNear with near: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [lon, lat] }, distanceField: 'distanceMeters', spherical: true, maxDistance: radius (lines 16-24).

checks.practice: When performing sphere-based geospatial queries, ensure GeoJSON coordinates are [lng, lat] and include spherical: true (or use the sphere-aware operator) so distances are computed on an earth-like sphere; use distanceMultiplier to convert units if needed.
checks.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js uses coordinates [lon, lat] and sets spherical: true in $geoNear (lines 18,21).

checks.practice: Project only the fields the client needs (limit returned fields such as location, distance, hours, stock) to reduce network payload and RU/I/O consumption.
checks.evidence: $project stage in app/src/routes/nearby.js lists only name, location, opening_hours, stock, distanceMeters (lines 26-32).

checks.practice: Use pagination (limit + skip or range-based cursors) for large result sets and avoid unbounded queries to prevent resource overconsumption and huge responses.
checks.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js runs aggregation without limit or pagination (no limit/skip or cursor usage; line 36 returns all results).
checks.fix: Add limit and optional page/cursor parameters to /nearby (e.g., ?limit=50&after=<cursor> or ?page=1&limit=25). If returning large lists, use a cursor-based approach to avoid skip for large offsets.

checks.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and on rate-limited responses (HTTP 429), and honor Retry-After headers when provided.
checks.evidence: No retry-with-backoff logic is present in repository; seed/verify and /nearby handler do not implement explicit retry behaviour.
checks.fix: Implement an application-level retry wrapper for transient errors and honor 429 Retry-After; or use driver-retry settings when appropriate. Add a small retry helper and use it around critical DB operations (with bounded attempts and exponential backoff).

checks.practice: Handle common driver and server errors (connection timeout, network errors, cursor timeouts, server 5xx) and return appropriate HTTP statuses from the API rather than leaking internal errors.
checks.evidence: The /nearby route returns 400 for missing numeric params (lines 12-14) and returns 500 for exceptions (lines 38-40). The code does not map specific DB error types to distinct HTTP statuses.
checks.fix: Enhance error handling to map known error classes (e.g., network/timeouts → 503, bad query → 400, unauthorized → 401) and avoid exposing internal traces in responses.

checks.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent: check existence or upsert documents and create indexes only if missing so the script can be safely re-run in CI/ops.
checks.evidence: seed/seed.js uses updateOne(..., { upsert: true }) to upsert each store (lines 23-26) and calls Store.createIndexes() (lines 29-31); build logs show idempotent run.

checks.practice: Monitor query performance and index usage (use explain('executionStats') or MCP explain_operation and ensure geospatial queries use a 2dsphere index rather than scanning the collection).
checks.evidence: No explain() usage or saved explain output in repo. Build did run a verify aggregation and the MCP list-indexes tool showed the 2dsphere index exists (events.jsonl), but no explain/executionStats are captured or logged.
checks.fix: Add an optional verify script or CI check that runs Store.aggregate([...]).explain('executionStats') and logs/records index usage; include this step in README for operators.

checks.practice: When using Mongoose in production, avoid enabling autoIndex; prefer controlled index builds as part of deployment.
checks.evidence: No explicit autoIndex configuration in app/src/index.js or package files; seed script creates indexes explicitly. A search for 'autoIndex' in repo returned no matches (events.jsonl). Public, Azure-DocumentDB-specific guidance about Mongoose autoIndex was not found by discovery.
checks.searched: Searches: 'Mongoose autoIndex Azure DocumentDB', 'Mongoose autoIndex documentdb', 'disable autoIndex production mongoose azure'
checks.fix: Provide a short, public guidance page in the agent kit or the documentdb-local-deployment skill describing recommended Mongoose autoIndex settings for production on Azure DocumentDB (set autoIndex:false in production and perform index builds via migration scripts).
checks.what_would_help: A sentence in a 'Mongoose on Azure DocumentDB' page stating: 'Disable autoIndex in production (autoIndex:false) and create indexes explicitly during deployment.'

checks.practice: Validate and sanitize latitude/longitude input ranges (lat between -90 and 90, lon between -180 and 180) and enforce a reasonable maximum radius for geospatial queries to prevent abusive or expensive queries.
checks.evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js validates numeric presence (NaN) but does not enforce lat/lon ranges or a maximum radius (lines 8-14). Discovery did not find an Azure-DocumentDB-specific public guidance page for lat/lon validation.
checks.searched: Searches: 'validate lat lon input azure documentdb', 'sanitize geospatial query radius best practice'
checks.fix: Publish a short 'API input validation' note in the agent kit showing allowed lat/lon ranges and recommending a default maximum radius (e.g., maxRadiusMeters=50000) and provide a code snippet.
checks.what_would_help: An authoritative short paragraph on the Geo queries page: 'Validate lat ∈ [-90,90], lon ∈ [-180,180], and clamp or reject radii above X meters (default X=50km)'.

checks.practice: Do not add vector indexes to collections that do not need them; keep vector and geo workloads separated into different collections when possible to avoid unnecessary storage and compute overhead.
checks.evidence: This sample does not create vector indexes; geo data is stored in a collection without vector indexes.

checks.practice: Provision cluster compute and storage according to workload: pick compute tier for IOPS/throughput and size storage for capacity.
checks.evidence: The sample is built to run against an existing cluster and does not provision resources; no IaC present to select tier/storage.
checks.fix: If providing IaC, include sensible default SKU (e.g., M30 free/dev default) and document scaling guidance.

checks.practice: Avoid starting long-running or blocking index builds during peak traffic; run index builds during maintenance windows or use the provider’s recommended background/online build options.
checks.evidence: Seed script calls createIndexes in a one-off script; sample does not attempt large index builds at runtime.
checks.fix: Document index build considerations in README if sample grows to include large datasets.

checks.practice: Give indexes meaningful names and include index definitions in deployment manifests or migration scripts so operators can reconcile indexes created by the app versus ops tooling.
checks.evidence: Schema index is defined but no explicit index name or deployment manifest is provided; created index appears as default name location_2dsphere (events.jsonl documentdb_list_indexes output).
checks.fix: Include an index-creation script or deployment manifest that names the index explicitly and add it to repo (e.g., createIndexes command with name and options).

checks.practice: Log aggregation pipelines and explain() output in non-sensitive debugging logs when diagnosing query performance, but avoid logging connection strings, credentials, or other secrets.
checks.evidence: No logging of aggregation pipeline or explain() output in repo; morgan is enabled (app/src/index.js line 8) but no debug logging of aggregation/explain output is present.
checks.fix: Add an optional verbose debug mode (controlled by env var) that logs the pipeline and, when enabled, runs explain('executionStats') and logs the result to non-sensitive logs.

checks.practice: For local development using the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image, connect on port 10260 with TLS and, if necessary for local self-signed certs, relax validation only under explicit env control (tlsAllowInvalidCertificates), but never default to relaxed TLS in code.
checks.evidence: This run used a reachable live cluster; repository does not include Docker local gateway instructions.
checks.fix: If adding local dev instructions, include example docker-compose and note port 10260 and TLS relax controlled by env var.

checks.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID with RBAC and customer-managed keys (CMK) for production clusters with compliance requirements rather than only long-lived passwords or default service-managed keys.
checks.evidence: README and sample code do not document or demonstrate Microsoft Entra ID authentication or explain why password-mode is used for the sample. The code accepts DOCUMENTDB_URI but doesn't show Entra ID usage examples.
checks.fix: Add a README section explaining Entra ID vs password authentication, and provide an example or link for using MONGODB-OIDC/Microsoft Entra ID for production clusters.

checks.practice: Use diagnostic settings and slow-query logs (export to Log Analytics) and alert on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage and connection saturation per cluster tier to detect resource pressure early.
checks.evidence: Sample is a small demo and does not configure diagnostic settings or alerting for clusters in repo.
checks.fix: If providing production deployment IaC, add guidance and example diagnostic settings and alert rules.

checks.practice: The driver version is pinned and is one the service supports.
checks.evidence: The repo contains package-lock.json (locks installed versions). package.json uses caret ranges (app/package.json lines 15-19) but package-lock.json pins resolved driver versions used during build (package-lock.json present). Official quickstart docs list tested driver versions and Mongoose compatibility.
checks.searched: Searched Microsoft Learn quickstart for Mongoose/driver tested versions (learn.microsoft.com quickstart-nodejs-mongoose).
checks.fix: Prefer explicit pinned versions in package.json for samples or mention in README which exact package-lock versions are tested. Smallest fix: add a 'Tested with' line in README pointing at the package-lock.json-resolved versions.

sources.title: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with 'ready_with_gaps' is an operator decision. Events show build proceeded with gaps noted; evidence supports the decision.
Choice to use Node.js with Mongoose is exactly what the prompt requested; events show Mongoose was installed and used (package.json, created files).

Choosing caret ^7.0.0 for Mongoose is a 'model_default' decision. The repo uses ^7.0.0 (package.json). Microsoft docs provide guidance on tested driver versions (Learn quickstart) so pinning an exact tested version would be preferable; the decision is defensible but not grounded in a specific doc at the time it was recorded.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment is implemented (src/index.js) and matches the run-environment guidance; events show .env.example created.
Decision not to provision resources matches run policy. No provisioning commands were run; events show no IaC attempt.
Keeping collection unsharded is a valid scope decision for a small demo. There is no sharding code in the repo, matching the decision.
Decision to create a 2dsphere index and not add additional indexes is implemented (models/store.js index and no other indexes).
Duplicate approval decision; consistent with D001.
Duplicate of earlier ODM choice; justified by prompt and implemented.
Duplicate of D004; reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from env is implemented and logged in events.

Decision to try MCP create_index and also include index in Mongoose model is supported by events: MCP create_index was attempted and the model includes the index. The tool call failed but the decision and its rationale were correct.

The intent to use MCP tools for verification was reasonable and the seed script was included, but the MCP create_index tool failed (events.jsonl shows ToolExecutionException). The decision relied on a tool that turned out to be opt-in/disabled in this environment; fallback was executed.
Decision to accept lat/lon/radius as query parameters is implemented (src/routes/nearby.js) and documented in README. Events show the route matches this API shape.

Fallback to creating the index via Mongoose after MCP tool failure is supported by events (documentdb_create_index tool failed twice; npm run seed created indexes; events.jsonl show 'Indexes ensured').

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No Azure-DocumentDB-specific public guidance on whether Mongoose autoIndex should be disabled in production (the discovery returned prior knowledge only).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searched installed skills and web for 'Mongoose autoIndex Azure DocumentDB' and repository search (events.jsonl search_text).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder did not disable autoIndex explicitly; seed script creates indexes but there is no explicit production configuration to disable autoIndex. Agents relying on memory may not disable autoIndex when they should.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Mongoose on Azure DocumentDB' doc: state that autoIndex should be disabled in production (autoIndex:false) and show the recommended pattern (create indexes in migration/seed scripts) with a code snippet and example env-based toggle. Include a 1-paragraph rationale and example Bicep/az CLI migration step.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public DocumentDB-specific guidance found during discovery on validating latitude/longitude ranges and enforcing max radius for geo endpoints.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searched skills and web: 'validate lat lon input azure documentdb', 'sanitize geospatial query radius best practice'.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The /nearby endpoint only checks numeric params (NaN) and does not clamp/reject out-of-range coordinates or limit max radius, leaving API vulnerable to expensive or abusive queries unless the developer adds safeguards.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short paragraph to the Geo queries page advising: validate lat ∈ [-90,90], lon ∈ [-180,180], enforce a default maximum radius (e.g., 50km), and include code snippets for server-side validation and returning 400 on invalid input.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Agent did not surface the official guidance about tested Mongoose/MongoDB driver versions by discovery; it was found only by name search. The quickstart docs do list tested driver versions.
doc_gaps.where_searched: learn.microsoft.com quickstart and tutorial pages for Mongoose + Azure DocumentDB (found by targeted search).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder used caret ranges in package.json but package-lock.json pinned versions for the build. Agents following default choices might not pick a driver version that the docs explicitly tested.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Make the 'Tested driver versions' and 'Recommended Mongoose/driver pairing' more visible on the quickstart/tutorial landing page; add one-line 'Tested with Mongoose X.Y.Z (MongoDB driver A.B.C)' near the top so agents find it by general search.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Samples and quickstarts mention connection options but a concise example of application-level retries (exponential backoff + honoring Retry-After) for the Node.js/Mongoose stack on DocumentDB was not prominent.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-connection skill and quickstart pages; discovery located general guidance but not a compact Node.js example.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: No retry logic was added to the sample; transient failures and HTTP 429s are not handled specifically by the API, increasing risk in real deployments.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Retries and backoff' example in the documentdb-connection skill: Node.js snippet showing a small retry wrapper (with exponential backoff) for DB operations and handling 429 with Retry-After. Include guidance when driver-level retries are sufficient vs when app-level retries are required.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: README did not include explicit cleanup steps nor guidance for running tests without a live cluster.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository README and quickstart; no cleanup or test instructions found.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users receiving the sample may not know how to remove the created sample data or run tests offline; it increases friction for CI and local experimentation.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Clean-up' section showing how to drop the stores collection (mongo shell or node snippet) and an optional 'Testing' section that shows how to run unit tests with mongodb-memory-server or mocks and what environment variables are required.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No example IaC template (Bicep/Terraform) showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource for vCore clusters was included.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repo and quickstart IaC; none in sample. Readiness findings noted agent confusion between databaseAccounts and mongoClusters.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Operators who try to supply infrastructure-as-code may target the wrong resource type (databaseAccounts) or leave out tier/storage parameters; this increases risk of incorrect provisioning.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a minimal Bicep template that creates Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameterized sku/tier and region, plus sample az CLI commands; add a short note clarifying difference from Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (RU-based Cosmos).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The MCP 'create_index' tool failed in this run with an opt-in requirement (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS). There was no repo-level note about MCP opt-in settings.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder attempted to use MCP create_index and the tool failed; they fell back to seed.createIndexes. Future builders/agents will retry the MCP tool unless informed about opt-in.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short agent-kit rule or README note: 'When using MCP management tools in this environment you may need to set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true; otherwise fall back to application-level index creation.'
